userStories.title: Add Core Web Vitals optimization: hero image priority and lazy-loading
userStories.description: The Hero component (Hero.tsx) likely uses a large banner image that is the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) element. Without the `priority` prop on the Next.js Image component, the hero image is lazy-loaded, causing LCP scores above 4s on mobile — a Google ranking signal. Additionally, below-fold images should be explicitly lazy-loaded and sized with the `sizes` attribute to prevent Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS). Target: LCP < 2.5s, CLS < 0.1.

userStories.description: Immersive per-room photo galleries with a keyboard-navigable lightbox are one of the top conversion drivers for boutique accommodation websites. Travellers who can inspect the dorm, private room, bathroom, and common areas in detail before booking show significantly higher booking confidence. Each room type page needs a dedicated gallery with at least 6 categorised photos.
acceptanceCriteria: Each room type page has a photo gallery with at least 6 images covering: bed/bunk, room overview, bathroom, window/view, storage, common area
Gallery is navigable via keyboard (arrow keys to cycle images, Escape to close lightbox)
Gallery images optimised via next/image with AVIF/WebP and correct `sizes` attribute
All gallery images have descriptive alt text, lightbox has a focus trap, close button is keyboard accessible
Gallery does not degrade LCP — hero image loads before gallery JS is initialised
Gallery uses Intersection Observer to lazy-initialise when scrolled into view
technicalNotes: Recommended: yet-another-react-lightbox (accessible, Next.js compatible, tree-shakeable)
Alternative: Radix UI Dialog for full accessibility control with custom gallery UI
Defer gallery initialisation using Intersection Observer — only load when component enters viewport
yet-another-react-lightbox: https://yet-another-react-lightbox.com/

userStories.title: Enable typedRoutes for compile-time Next.js link type-safety
userStories.description: Next.js supports `experimental.typedRoutes` which generates TypeScript types for all app routes at build time. Every `<Link href>` and `router.push()` call becomes type-checked, catching broken internal links before they reach production. Particularly valuable as the hostel site grows with new room pages, blog posts, and event pages.
acceptanceCriteria: `experimental: { typedRoutes: true }` set in next.config.ts
TypeScript compiler reports type errors for any `<Link href="/invalid-route">`
All existing valid `<Link>` hrefs type-check correctly with no false positives
CI pipeline runs `tsc --noEmit` to catch broken links on every PR
No build errors introduced by the typedRoutes feature
technicalNotes: Enable in next.config.ts: `experimental: { typedRoutes: true }`
Works with both Webpack and Turbopack build systems
Next.js docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/typedRoutes

userStories.title: Implement View Transitions API for animated page navigation
userStories.description: Next.js 15 exposes `experimental.viewTransition` which leverages the native browser View Transitions API for smooth, animated page transitions. For a hostel website, this creates polished cross-fade or slide animations when navigating between room pages, the gallery, and the blog — improving perceived performance and brand feel with zero third-party JS.
acceptanceCriteria: `experimental: { viewTransition: true }` enabled in next.config.ts
Navigation between room detail pages shows a cross-fade or slide transition animation
Navigation between blog post pages shows a smooth transition
Transitions respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no animation when reduced motion is preferred)
No layout shift or flash of unstyled content during transitions
Works correctly in Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Safari 18+
technicalNotes: Enable with `experimental: { viewTransition: true }` in next.config.ts
Add `::view-transition-old` / `::view-transition-new` CSS rules for custom animations
Pair with `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { * { animation-duration: 0.01ms !important; } }`
Next.js docs: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/viewTransition
